rendering.persona_description: Mateo is a 67-year-old retired machinist who spends his days restoring old radios in his garage workshop and keeping up a vegetable garden with raised beds he built himself. He's been married to his wife Carol for eleven years and transitioned in his late fifties, something he describes matter-of-factly as 'the one thing I got right on the first try.' He's practical, dry-humored, and prides himself on being able to fix almost anything with his hands.
rendering.clinical_context: Mateo has no mental-health presentation. Like most people, he sometimes has a passing thought about germs on public surfaces, doorknobs, or secondhand objects, and occasionally wipes something down or washes his hands a bit more carefully after handling mail. These moments come and go without lasting distress and without anything he does to neutralize them; he doesn't dwell on them, and they don't shape his day.
rendering.behavioral_description: Mateo talks in short, concrete sentences and tends to explain his reasoning like he's troubleshooting a machine, citing specific surfaces, specific illnesses, specific numbers of washes when the subject comes up. He pushes back when a suggestion sounds like it's asking him to just stop thinking a certain way, but he'll consider a reframe if it's presented as a fact he hadn't weighed rather than a command. He'll mention offhand that he wiped down a doorknob or washed his hands after the mail, the same way he'd mention checking the oil in his truck, and moves on without circling back to it.

traits.living_situation: lives with his wife in a single-family home
traits.help_seeking_orientation: sees no need for professional input; would consider a specific, factual suggestion but isn't looking for reassurance about anything in particular
traits.cognitive_style: literal, detail-focused, reasons by analogy to physical systems

clinical_history.current_treatment: none currently; he has never started formal treatment for these symptoms
clinical_history.history: No history of any mental-health condition. Like most people, he has ordinary passing thoughts now and then, including about germs or cleanliness, that come and go without lasting distress and without anything done to neutralize them.
